summary: The study investigates the deposition of superconducting Nb-N thin films using metal-organic plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD). The process involves the use of (tert-butylimido)-tris(diethylamino)-niobium (TBTDEN) and hydrogen plasma as precursors. The effects of plasma parameters, such as hydrogen flow rate and plasma dose time, on the superconducting properties, including transition temperature (TC) and critical current density (JC), are analyzed. The films exhibit superconductivity with TC values ranging from 6.2 K to 14 K, and the highest TC and JC values are achieved with optimized plasma parameters. The films consist of polycrystalline Nb-N with amorphous or microcrystalline niobium oxide and oxy-nitride phases. The study highlights the potential of these films for superconducting nanowire single photon detectors (SNSPDs).
